definition: The lived body understood not as a Cartesian object among objects but as the subject of perception and action — the body-subject constantly responds to the world through an 'I can' rather than an 'I think,' constituting an irreducible third term between mind and matter that dissolves the classical dualism of consciousness and mechanism
connective_patterns: the body-subject characterized by I can rather than I think
the body-subject as the third term beyond mind and matter
the body-subject's intentional arc toward the world

definition: The body as experienced from within — not the anatomical body of physiology but the body as it is lived, felt, and practically engaged with the world; the lived body (corps propre/corps vécu) emphasizes the co-penetration of subject and world from a first-person perspective, functioning as the medium through which we inhabit and make sense of our environment
connective_patterns: the lived body as medium of world-engagement
the lived body as first-person perspective
the co-penetration of lived body and lived space

definition: Not a mental state or inner representation but the organism's entire bodily activity in relation to its environment — to perceive is to be familiar with, deal with, and find one's way around in a world; perception is primary and pre-predicative, preceding and grounding all conceptual and scientific thought, constituting the primordial opening to being
connective_patterns: the primacy of perception
to perceive is to inhabit a world
perception as pre-predicative openness to being

definition: An elemental, universal texture of Being that is neither pure matter nor pure consciousness — the flesh (la chair) is the medium through which all things, subjects, and objects are interrelated; it is the sensory stratum shared between seer and seen, toucher and touched, the ontological fabric that makes reversibility and the chiasm possible
connective_patterns: flesh as the element of Being
flesh as neither matter nor mind
the thickness of flesh between seer and thing is their means of communication

definition: The crossing or intertwining structure by which subject and world, visible and invisible, seer and seen are reciprocally inserted into each other — the chiasm (le chiasme) expresses Merleau-Ponty's non-dualistic ontology in which opposites are not separate substances but aspects of a single folding, like the two sides of a leaf or the crossing of hands
connective_patterns: the chiasm of visible and invisible
the chiasm as reciprocal insertion of subject and world
the chiasm as the structure of the flesh

definition: The fundamental structure of embodied perception whereby the perceiver and the perceived belong to the same ontological fabric — demonstrated paradigmatically by the touching hands: the right hand that touches the left is simultaneously touched by it, so that the touching and the touched are always on the verge of exchanging roles without ever fully coinciding
connective_patterns: the reversibility of touching and touched
reversibility as always imminent but never fully achieved
reversibility as the fundamental of the flesh

definition: A form of understanding that irreducibly involves bodily set and preparation — distinct from the act intentionality of judgments, motor intentionality is the body's pre-reflective directedness toward objects and tasks, grasping the meaning of a situation through practical engagement rather than conceptual representation, as when a hand shapes itself to grasp before any conscious decision
connective_patterns: motor intentionality as the body's I can
motor intentionality distinct from act intentionality
the body understands through motor intentionality

definition: The pre-reflective, dynamic system of motor capacities, postural adjustments, and habitual dispositions that constitutes the body's practical grasp of its situation — not a conscious image or map of the body but an implicit, operative understanding that integrates the body's parts into a unified field of action oriented toward the world
connective_patterns: the body schema as pre-reflective motor competence
the body schema integrates parts into unified action
tools incorporated into the body schema

definition: The pre-objective domain of lived experience in which things first appear as meaningful — the phenomenal field is the field of perception prior to the abstractions of science and reflective thought, where figure and ground, near and far, self and world are structured by the body's practical engagement rather than by intellectual categories
connective_patterns: the phenomenal field as the domain of lived experience
return to the phenomenal field
the phenomenal field structures perception before reflection

term: visible and invisible/可见与不可见
definition: The paired dimensions of Merleau-Ponty's late ontology — the visible is not mere surface appearance but always carries within it an invisible lining (the depth, the horizon, the unseen sides of things); the invisible is not a separate realm but the latency, depth, and dimensionality that is constitutive of every visible presence, structuring perception from within
connective_patterns: every visible carries an invisible lining
the invisible as the depth-dimension of the visible
the intertwining of visible and invisible

definition: Entrelacs — the continuous weaving together of perceiver and perceived, touching and touched, subject and world in Merleau-Ponty's ontology of the flesh; intertwining names the way that opposites are not juxtaposed externally but folded into each other, each term enveloping the other without coinciding, creating the chiasmic structure of experience
connective_patterns: the intertwining of seer and seen
the intertwining as the structure of the chiasm
the intertwining of visible and invisible in perception

definition: Not merely the third dimension of geometric space but the primordial spatial dimension through which the world opens up as a field of presence — depth is the dimension in which things coexist in proximity and distance, making possible the phenomenon of perceptual perspective; it is the first dimension because it is the dimension of the lived body's engagement with a surrounding world
connective_patterns: depth as the primordial dimension of perception
depth as the dimension of coexistence
depth reveals the body's being-in-the-world

definition: A form of bodily knowledge that cannot be reduced to either mechanical reflexes or intellectual representations — habit is the body's capacity to incorporate new skills and extend its motor repertoire through practice, restructuring the body schema to encompass tools, instruments, and environments as extensions of the body's own practical field
connective_patterns: habit as bodily knowledge beyond mechanism and intellect
habit extends the body schema
tools incorporated through habit become extensions of the body

definition: The constitutive indeterminacy of embodied existence — ambiguity is not a defect of description but the essential character of the lived body, which is simultaneously subject and object, active and passive, nature and culture; Merleau-Ponty's philosophy embraces ambiguity as the fundamental truth of human being rather than seeking to resolve it into clear and distinct categories
connective_patterns: ambiguity as the essential character of embodied existence
the lived body as the exemplary locus of ambiguity
embracing ambiguity rather than resolving it
